A low shaft of green-gold morning light through the opening, landing square on the counter and lighting the dust and every phial-rim in its path, the rest of the room a warm amber dusk behind it.

Lamplight passing through a row of coloured glass bottles and laying soft pools of emerald, rose and amber along the counter-top, the shelves beyond them sinking into deep umber, the ceiling lost in warm brown.

A single jar of luminous spores glowing from inside its shelf-bay, its cold blue-green light underlighting the shelf above and throwing every bundle's shadow upward, the rest of the room amber with lamp-warmth against it.

A beeswax lamp hung low over the counter, its warm circle falling on the work-surface below while the crowded shelves recede into soft brown shadow and the gill-flesh ceiling holds a dull amber warmth above.

Late honey-coloured afternoon light raking sideways across the gill-flesh ceiling and picking out every pleat and fold, the shelves below held in warm shade, the glassware catching amber and throwing it back in bright flecks.

The glow of a small brazier underlighting a copper still, warming the underside of every hanging bundle above it, the whole room a deep russet-amber shot through with the copper's hot orange-red at its centre.

Cool blue dusk filling the opening while a lamp holds the counter warm, both colours meeting across the floor in a slow tide, the nearest jars glowing gold and those toward the door gone deep slate-blue.

Rain-grey light flattening the opening, flat and colourless, while the lamplight makes every crowded jar glow like a sweet — emerald, ruby, amber — the shelves jewelled against the grey dull square of the door.

A narrow slant of afternoon sun through a gap overhead landing on the floorboards in a soft-edged warm patch, the counter above it in shadow, the jars on the lowest shelf catching gold along their shoulders.

Light bouncing up off a pale stoneware basin, filling the shadows under the shelves with diffuse cool-white brightness, the upper room amber with lamp-glow, the two meeting at mid-shelf in a soft line of contrast.

The last rose-amber of sunset laid along the top shelf alone, the bottles there glowing ruby and gold while everything below sinks into deep warm dusk, the floor nearly dark, the ceiling still faintly rose.

Morning mist-light coming in flat and pearl-pale through the opening, gentling every colour in the room, the jars reading soft jade, blush and cream, the lamp still lit and pooling weak gold at the counter.

A cluster of glow-worm lanterns above the loft rail dropping soft green-white light down the ladder, the loft floor glowing faintly above, the main room below amber with its own lamp, the two greens and golds layered.

Firelight throwing the shadows of the hanging bundles up the curved wall in broad warm shapes, the wall itself cycling between deep ochre and near-black as the fire breathes, the jars lit orange along their nearest edges.

A shaft of hazy noon light finding the hand-blown glass of one tall bottle and pulling a soft green patch on the gill-flesh wall behind it, the rest of the room even and bright, every shelf colour reading clean.

A single candle-lamp on the counter, the room reduced to amber close in and deep umber beyond, only the nearest jars readable — one streak of ruby, one of old gold — the far shelves given to warm dark.

Warm amber light leaking up through the gaps in the loft floor and spreading across the ceiling above in soft irregular patches, the room below lamp-lit and deep amber, the ceiling above patterned with dull glowing seams.
Noon light flooding in white and even through the opening so every colour on the shelves reads at once — emerald, sapphire, amber, deep rose — the room bright and full, every shadow shallow and warm.

A lamp set behind the crowded shelves so the jars glow from within and the shelf-fronts go dark silhouette, each bottle a lit jewel of amber or green against the black plank edge, the counter beyond in warm dusk.

The cold clear light after rain coming in sharp and pale through the opening, washing the counter almost white, every wet-glass surface picking up a hard clean highlight, the back of the room still holding lamp-amber warmth.

Low sun at the day's end catching only the underside of the cap-ceiling and leaving the shelves in warm shade below, the ceiling a saturated amber-gold overhead, the jars readable only by the lamplight pooled at the counter.

A handful of drifting luminous spores crossing the dark of the room, each leaving a brief soft blue-green smear on the air, the lamp at the counter still amber and steady, the two lights utterly unlike each other.

Pearl-pale mist-morning light sitting flat in the opening, the lamp still burning on the counter and throwing a warm gold pool onto the worn wood, the whole room caught between cool silver-grey at the door and amber within.

A lamp behind a tall amber bottle on the back shelf, the bottle glowing like a coal, a streak of deep gold thrown across the counter-top, the room otherwise in soft brown dusk with the ceiling lost above.

Grey rain-light and early lamps together, the opening a cool pewter square, the interior a warm corridor of amber and jewel-colour — ruby jars, a streak of sapphire on the counter, the gill-flesh ceiling soaking up the lamp-glow to pale gold.
